sources.entry: Vafa - Open-source VPN kill switch that freezes chosen apps and blocks their network until a VPN with an allowed exit country is up. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/k33ssa/vafa) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Vafa is a free, open-source VPN kill switch for macOS and Windows that freezes chosen apps and blocks their network until a VPN with an allowed exit country is detected.
summary.what_it_does: Vafa runs a system daemon (root on macOS, a SYSTEM scheduled task on Windows) that checks the VPN every second and immediately on network changes. The VPN counts only when internet traffic goes through a tunnel adapter and Cloudflare, queried through that tunnel, reports an exit country outside the configured blocked list (Russia, China, Belarus and Iran by default). When the VPN is missing, it closes network access to protected hosts (Anthropic networks and telemetry by default) using pf on macOS or a Windows Firewall rule, freezes the chosen apps (or quits them with ON_DOWN=kill), and removes execute permission from app binaries so they cannot launch. A menu bar or tray shield shows the state and lets you pick apps and blocked countries. Claude Code CLI installs are also frozen on macOS by developer signature. Settings are kept across updates, and the README describes a separate unlock command to disable protection.
use_cases: stop apps from running or reaching the internet when the VPN is off
keep Claude or Claude Code from connecting without a VPN
block apps from exiting in certain countries
automatically freeze apps on VPN drop
enforce a VPN kill switch on macOS or Windows
protect against traffic leaking when a VPN reconnects
how_to_run: cd ~ && git clone <repo-url> && cd vafa && ./app/build.sh && sudo ./install.sh  (build from source on macOS)
Windows: unzip Vafa-1.0.3-windows.zip, then double-click install.cmd and allow the UAC prompt
stack: Wintun, WireGuard, OpenVPN and other tunnel adapters recognised by name
notable: Country check goes only through the VPN tunnel by IP, never from the real address
Network to protected hosts is closed by default at startup and during re-checks
Claude Code CLI freezing on macOS works by developer signature, covering npm, Homebrew, native and Claude.app copies
Windows service includes a watchdog that restarts the daemon if it crashes or hangs
Settings and app selection survive updates; Homebrew upgrades keep protection on since 1.0.1
caveats: Windows does not support system-proxy VPN mode; it needs a tunnel (TUN) mode VPN
Split tunneling that sends protected hosts outside the tunnel is treated as no VPN, so apps get blocked
Updating from version 1.0.0 on macOS briefly lifts protection for a few seconds
Requires the admin password on install because the daemon runs as root; Windows install needs UAC approval
